clues.text: While Paul waited here for Silas and Timothy, he was deeply disturbed to see the city full of idols.
Paul told the crowd he had found an altar here inscribed TO AN UNKNOWN GOD.
Epicurean and Stoic philosophers here debated with Paul and called him a babbler pushing foreign gods.
People who lived here, locals and foreigners alike, spent their time hearing and telling new ideas.
After Paul spoke at the Areopagus here, Dionysius and a woman named Damaris believed.
On his travels, Paul left this city and went on to the city of Corinth.
Paul told the Thessalonians that, unable to bear it any longer, he was willing to be left alone here.
